rule: After V36 builds its unchanged joint-bounded and speed-slewed position references, derive each reference rate from the current and preceding reference and existing sample-time interval. Clamp the derived rate to the unchanged selected actuator speed cap. Use zero rate on the initial command, whose reference remains neutral. Add reference-rate feedforward and reference-relative damping to the geometric angular-velocity command, then apply the existing speed clamp and motor direction sign.

formula.coefficient_basis: 1 + existing rate damping 0.65, derived for a velocity-output servo, not fitted from a successful outcome.
formula.first_command: Existing first reference and motor command; reference_rate=0.
formula.final_command: Existing selected speed clamp and motor direction sign -1.0.

scope: All eight hip/knee commands of the explicitly selected V37 resumed-walking controller only. No new force estimate, body impulse, transform write or observer input. Existing support-reference memory supplies time and previous references; no history reconstruction or session reset.
preserve: V36 floor provenance, feasible-height plan, smooth swing goals, joint bounds and reference slew
existing contact release/recontact gates, synchronization, dwell, timeout and seed
V20 recovery, stance V7, BW5R-B prefix and their exact commands
position gain 8.0, rate damping 0.65, actuator speed/force limits and all safety guards
neutral initial reference and first motor command
all old profile, memory and receipt bytes, with new optional mode/velocity receipt fields omitted for old policies
original evaluator, physical schedule, 400-command walking budget, 986-step tail and 1338-step child cap
required_receipt: Distinct V37 top-level actuation receipt and memory identities, plus reference_velocity_mode_id and ordered_reference_velocity_rad_s inside the support receipt. Preserve final clamps and their truthful saturation flags.
required_zero_world_checks: Core registration, ideal velocity-servo algebra, finite-rate bounds and first-command neutrality
Same-input V36 comparison: identical position goals, slewed references, feasible plans, phase/gate memory and limits; only the declared velocity-control outputs and distinct identities may differ
400 saved V36 inputs through real exported stateless and session calls with exact session/stateless output equality
Every saved-input derived reference rate and final motor velocity independently reconstructed
Byte-exact older-policy outputs and original recovery fixtures, runtime source binding and non-runnable component selection
risks: Existing velocity caps are reached more often in saved-input algebra; stronger movement may worsen support or attitude.
Finite differences respond to changes in the observed-pose-dependent reference; rate caps bound values but do not prove smooth native acceleration.
An ideal velocity actuator argument omits real torque limits, contact coupling, compliance and integration delay.
Stance interruptions, insufficient foot relocation and incomplete scheduled-cycle coverage may remain.
